subject: environmental-science
title: Malthus, Boserup and Sen
welcome_lead: Three economists, three views on whether population outruns resources.
meta_desc: A-Level Environmental Science adventure on Malthus, Boserup and Sen's capabilities approach.
final_note: Whether scarcity bites depends not just on numbers but on institutions and capabilities.

concepts.def: 18th-century economist: population grows geometrically, food arithmetically — leading to misery.
Malthusian famine, war and disease that raise mortality.
Malthusian moral restraint reducing birth rates.
Necessity drives innovation: population pressure stimulates agricultural intensification.
Famines result from entitlement failures, not absolute food shortage.
Sen's framework: development is expansion of substantive freedoms.

walkthroughs.body_html: Malthus saw inevitable collision between exponential population and linear food. The Industrial Revolution and Green Revolution postponed his prediction.
Boserup argued necessity drove innovation: shifting from extensive to intensive agriculture as populations grew.
Sen showed Bengal 1943 famine occurred amid normal supply — entitlement collapse, not crop failure, was decisive.

options: Population pressure drives agricultural innovation
Famine is inevitable as numbers grow
Birth rates always exceed death rates
Trade prevents scarcity
